mcq.q: Where should you shelter during a thunderstorm?
mcq.explanation: Lightning can strike tall trees, so a building is safer.

mcq.q: If there is no pavement, which side of the road should a pedestrian walk on?
options: In the middle of the road
The side facing the oncoming traffic
On the side where there is no light
mcq.explanation: Facing traffic lets you see vehicles coming towards you.

mcq.q: Which season usually follows the long rains in Kenya's common pattern?
mcq.explanation: In the usual pattern, June to August is cool or cold in many places.

mcq.q: Which of these places is likely to be coldest in Kenya?
mcq.explanation: High places are colder than low places.

mcq.q: Which of these is most likely to happen in the rainy season?
options: Herders move very far for water
mcq.explanation: Rain fills rivers and streams.

mcq.q: Which disease can spread more easily in wet weather because mosquitoes breed in puddles?
mcq.explanation: Mosquitoes that spread malaria breed in standing water.

mcq.q: How can you keep safe from the sun in the hot season?
options: Stay in the sun all day
Wear a hat, drink water and rest in the shade
Play in the hottest part of the day
mcq.explanation: These habits protect us from heat.

mcq.q: Why do farmers plan their work using seasons?
options: Seasons tell the price of clothes
Crops need the right weather to grow and be harvested
Seasons decide the colour of soil
mcq.explanation: Planting and harvesting depend on rain and dry weather.

mcq.q: Why should a weather chart be filled in at the same time each day?
options: So that the records can be compared fairly
So that the chart looks big
So that the sun rises earlier
mcq.explanation: Observing at the same time gives fair comparisons.

mcq.q: What is a historic built environment?
options: A place built long ago that tells us about the past
mcq.explanation: Historic built places are old places made by people.

mcq.q: What is a museum?
options: A place where crops are grown
A building where old objects are kept and shown
mcq.explanation: Museums keep artefacts safely and show them to people.

mcq.q: What is an artefact?
options: An object made and used by people in the past
mcq.explanation: Artefacts include tools, pots and clothes.

mcq.q: What is a monument?
options: A structure built to remember a person or event
mcq.explanation: Monuments remind people of important people or events.

mcq.q: What is a cultural centre?
options: A place where the culture of communities is shown and kept alive
mcq.explanation: Cultural centres show dances, homes, crafts and foods.

mcq.q: Fort Jesus is found in which town?
mcq.explanation: Fort Jesus is a fort at Mombasa.

mcq.q: Who built Fort Jesus?
mcq.explanation: The Portuguese built the fort more than 400 years ago.

mcq.q: Why was Fort Jesus built?
mcq.explanation: It was built as a stone fort to guard the harbour.

mcq.q: Which place in Nairobi shows traditional homes and dances of many communities?
mcq.explanation: The Bomas of Kenya is a cultural centre in Nairobi.

mcq.q: Which is a very old town on the Kenyan coast with narrow streets and stone houses?
mcq.explanation: Lamu Old Town is one of the oldest towns on the coast.

mcq.q: Thimlich Ohinga is found in which county?
mcq.explanation: Thimlich Ohinga is in Migori County.

mcq.q: Gede Ruins are near which coastal town?
mcq.explanation: Gede Ruins are near Watamu in Kilifi County.

mcq.q: Which monument in Nairobi remembers Kenya's independence in 1963?
mcq.explanation: Uhuru Gardens is where the Kenyan flag was first raised at independence.

mcq.q: What is the name of the organisation that looks after most museums in Kenya?
mcq.explanation: The National Museums of Kenya manages many museums.

mcq.q: What does UNESCO do for important old places?
mcq.explanation: UNESCO names World Heritage Sites and helps to protect them.

mcq.q: Which of these actions harms a historic place?
mcq.explanation: Writing on old walls spoils them.

mcq.q: Which of these actions helps to conserve a historic place?
mcq.explanation: Reporting damage helps protect the place.

mcq.q: Why do tourists visit historic places?
options: To learn about the past and enjoy the sights
mcq.explanation: Tourism brings income to the local people.

mcq.q: How can a historic place help a county to earn money?
options: By bringing visitors who pay fees and buy things
mcq.explanation: Visitors spend money on tickets, guides and crafts.

mcq.q: What should you do when visiting a museum?
options: Listen to the guide and do not touch objects unless allowed
mcq.explanation: Good manners protect the objects and other visitors.

mcq.q: Which of these is a service learning activity at a historic site?
mcq.explanation: Cleaning up is a way of serving and conserving.

mcq.q: What is the difference between a museum and a cultural centre?
options: A museum mainly keeps objects, a cultural centre shows living culture
A cultural centre has no dances
mcq.explanation: Cultural centres let visitors see and take part in living culture.

mcq.q: Which of these is not a historic built environment?
mcq.explanation: A river is a natural feature, not built by people.

mcq.q: Which is the best source of information about a historic place near you?
options: A resource person such as an elder or a guide
mcq.explanation: Elders and guides know the true story of the place.

mcq.q: What does interdependence mean?
options: People needing and helping each other
mcq.explanation: Interdependence means we depend on each other.

mcq.q: Why can no person do every job alone?
options: There are too many skills and jobs to learn
mcq.explanation: Nobody can grow all food, teach, heal and build alone.

mcq.q: What do traders do for farmers?
options: Buy their crops and take them to markets
mcq.explanation: Traders buy from farmers and sell in towns.

mcq.q: Which of these is a service?
mcq.explanation: A service is work done for someone. The others are goods.

mcq.q: Which of these is a good?
mcq.explanation: Goods are things we can touch and use.

mcq.q: What is barter?
options: Exchanging one thing for another without money
mcq.explanation: Barter means swapping goods, such as a goat for grain.

mcq.q: What is trade?
mcq.explanation: Trade is buying and selling.

mcq.q: Why do health workers depend on farmers?
options: Farmers grow the food they eat
mcq.explanation: Everyone needs food, including nurses and doctors.

mcq.q: Which group depends on teachers?
mcq.explanation: Teachers help children learn to read and write, which everybody needs.

mcq.q: What is harambee?
options: Working together to solve a problem
mcq.explanation: Harambee means pulling together.

mcq.q: Which of these shows interdependence?
options: Farmer sells maize and buys clothes from a tailor
mcq.explanation: The farmer and tailor depend on each other.

mcq.q: A tailor makes uniforms and a farmer buys them. What does the tailor need from the farmer?
options: Food or money from selling food
mcq.explanation: The tailor depends on the farmer for food.

mcq.q: Which place is used mainly for prayers and worship?
mcq.explanation: Places of worship are for prayer.

mcq.q: How do religious leaders help the community?
options: They teach values and comfort people
mcq.explanation: Religious leaders teach good values and care for people.

mcq.q: Who brings medicine and equipment to hospitals?
mcq.explanation: Transport workers carry goods to hospitals.

mcq.q: What is one benefit of interdependence?
options: We get goods and services we cannot make ourselves
mcq.explanation: Sharing skills gives us more goods and services.

mcq.q: Which is a way of showing appreciation for others?
mcq.explanation: Thanking people shows we value them.

mcq.q: What might happen if all drivers stopped working?
options: Food and medicine could not reach shops and hospitals
mcq.explanation: Transport connects producers, shops and hospitals.

mcq.q: In a chart of who gives and who needs, what does a farmer give?
mcq.explanation: Farmers give food to the community.

mcq.q: In a chart of who gives and who needs, what does a nurse give?
mcq.explanation: Nurses give health care.

mcq.q: Who helps at weddings and funerals in many communities?
mcq.explanation: People help by cooking, lending items and comforting.

mcq.q: Which statement is true?
mcq.explanation: Every worker contributes to the community.

mcq.q: How is money useful in trade?
options: It makes buying and selling easier
mcq.explanation: Money is a common way of paying for goods and services.

mcq.q: What is population?
options: The number of people living in a place
The number of animals in a place
mcq.explanation: Population is the number of people in an area.

mcq.q: What does population distribution mean?
options: How people are spread out in an area
How many trees are in an area
mcq.explanation: Distribution is about where people live.

mcq.q: What do we call an area where many people live close together?
mcq.explanation: Dense means crowded.

mcq.q: What do we call an area where few people live in a large space?
mcq.explanation: Sparse means thinly spread.

mcq.q: On a dot map, what does a group of many dots close together show?
mcq.explanation: Many dots show many people.

mcq.q: On a dot map where one dot means 1,000 people, an area has 7 dots. How many people live there?
On a dot map where one dot means 500 people, an area has 4 dots. How many people live there?
Which area is most likely to be sparsely populated?
options: A very dry area with little rain
mcq.explanation: Dry areas make farming and water supply hard.

mcq.q: Which is a reason why many people live in towns?
mcq.explanation: Towns offer work and services.

mcq.q: Which is a reason why fewer people live in a forest reserve?
options: People are not allowed to settle there
mcq.explanation: Forest reserves are protected.

mcq.q: Why do many people live near rivers and lakes?
options: Water is available for drinking and farming
mcq.explanation: Water is a basic need.

mcq.q: Which pattern describes people living along a road or river in a line?
mcq.explanation: Linear means in a line.

mcq.q: Which pattern describes houses standing close together around a trading centre?
mcq.explanation: Clustered means close together in a group.

mcq.q: Which pattern describes each family living far from the next on its own land?
mcq.explanation: Scattered means spread widely apart.

mcq.q: Which of these counties has a very dense city population?
mcq.explanation: Nairobi has a large city population.

mcq.q: Which type of area in Kenya usually has few people for its size?
options: Dry areas in the far north
mcq.explanation: Dry northern areas are sparsely populated.

mcq.q: Why do herders in dry areas not live crowded in one place?
options: They move with animals to look for water and grass
mcq.explanation: Herding needs large areas of pasture.

mcq.q: Which is the best way to show population on a map using dots?
options: Draw dots where people live and give a key for what a dot means
mcq.explanation: A dot map needs a clear key.

mcq.q: Why must a key be included on a dot map?
options: So that the map is longer
So that people know what each dot stands for
mcq.explanation: Without a key we cannot read the dots.

mcq.q: In a bar graph of sub-county populations, which sub-county has the tallest bar?
options: The one with the fewest people
The one with the most people
mcq.explanation: Taller bars show bigger values.

mcq.q: In a shaded map, which shade usually shows the most crowded area?
mcq.explanation: Dark shades show higher numbers.

mcq.q: Why is population distribution useful to county planners?
options: It helps them to grow tea
It helps them to place schools, clinics and roads where people live
It helps them to change the weather
It helps them to move rivers
mcq.explanation: Services should reach people where they live.

mcq.q: Which of these is not a reason for crowded areas?
options: Very little rain and no water
mcq.explanation: Dryness with no water makes areas sparse.

mcq.q: What is culture?
options: The way of life of a community
mcq.explanation: Culture is the way of life passed on from generation to generation.

mcq.q: Who usually passes traditional culture on to children?
mcq.explanation: Culture is taught in families and communities.

mcq.q: Which of these is an aspect of traditional culture?
mcq.explanation: Dressing, food, housing, artefacts, games and ceremonies are aspects of culture.

mcq.q: Which is a traditional food eaten in many parts of Kenya?
mcq.explanation: Ugali is widely eaten in Kenya.

mcq.q: Which food is made of maize and beans mixed together?
mcq.explanation: Githeri is maize and beans.

mcq.q: Which cloth is a printed cloth worn especially at the Kenyan coast?
mcq.explanation: The kanga is printed cloth popular on the coast.

mcq.q: Which of these is a Maasai red or blue checked cloth?
mcq.explanation: The shuka is a checked cloth worn by the Maasai.

mcq.q: In traditional culture, what do we call a basket or clay pot made and used by people?
mcq.explanation: Baskets and pots are artefacts.

short.q: Explain why a monument is built.
short.answer: A monument is built to remind people of an important person or event so that they remember it.
short.working: 1 mark for reminding people, 1 mark for the idea of a person or event.

short.q: Give three reasons why historic built environments are important.
short.answer: They teach us history, they give us identity and pride, and they bring tourists and income.

short.q: Explain how a cultural centre is different from a museum.
short.answer: A museum mainly keeps and shows objects. A cultural centre lets people see and join in living culture such as dances and crafts. Some places do both.
short.working: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

short.q: List four rules that visitors should follow at a historic place.
short.answer: Do not litter, do not write on walls, do not climb or touch old structures, and listen to the guide.

short.q: Describe three ways in which pupils can take part in conserving a historic place near their school.
short.answer: Sweep and pick up litter, report damage to an adult, and tell others why the place is important.

short.q: Explain how a historic place such as Fort Jesus helps local people to earn a living.
short.answer: Visitors pay entry fees, guides are employed, hotels and restaurants get customers, and craft sellers sell to tourists.

short.q: Write a short note to invite a resource person to talk about a historic place in your county. Include the reason and the date.
short.answer: A polite greeting, the name of the person, the reason for the invitation, the date and time, and a thank-you at the end.
short.working: 1 mark for each of the five parts.

short.q: Describe how you would prepare for a class visit to a museum, and what you would do during the visit.
short.answer: Ask permission from the teacher and the museum, prepare questions, take a notebook, stay with the group, listen to the guide, take notes and do not touch objects.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct point, up to 5.

short.q: Explain what interdependence means and give one example.
short.answer: Interdependence means people depend on and help each other. For example, a farmer grows food and a trader sells it.
short.working: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example, 1 mark for showing both sides need each other.

short.q: Give two examples of goods and two examples of services.
short.answer: Goods: maize and shoes. Services: teaching and nursing.

short.q: Explain how a farmer and a trader depend on each other.
short.answer: The farmer grows crops and sells them to the trader. The trader carries the crops to town and sells them. The trader needs the crops and the farmer needs the buyer.

short.q: State three benefits of interdependence in a county.
short.answer: People get goods and services they cannot make, people help each other in trouble, and the county develops faster.

short.q: Describe how health workers, farmers and teachers depend on each other.
short.answer: Health workers keep farmers and teachers well. Farmers give food to health workers and teachers. Teachers teach the children of farmers and health workers. Each group needs the others to live well.

short.q: Explain what harambee is and give one example of what it can be used for.
short.answer: Harambee is people pulling together to solve a problem, for example to build a school or a clinic.
short.working: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example.

short.q: Explain two ways of showing appreciation to people who help us.
short.answer: Say thank you and treat their work with respect. Accept helping them in return.

short.q: Draw a simple chart showing three workers, what each gives, and what each needs.
short.answer: For example: farmer gives food and needs clothes; teacher gives learning and needs food; driver gives transport and needs repairs.

short.q: Explain what would happen in a community if farmers stopped growing food.
short.answer: There would be a shortage of food. Traders would have nothing to sell. Prices would go up. People could become hungry and ill.

short.q: Give five people who serve your community and say how each helps.
short.answer: For example: farmer grows food, teacher teaches, nurse treats the sick, driver carries people and goods, trader sells goods.
short.working: 1 mark for each person with a correct service.

short.q: Explain the meaning of population distribution.
short.answer: It is how the people are spread out over an area, showing where many people live and where few live.
short.working: 1 mark for spread of people, 1 mark for many and few.

short.q: Give two reasons why some areas are densely populated.
short.answer: Good rain and fertile soil for farming, and jobs and services in towns. Accept water or good roads.

short.q: Give two reasons why some areas are sparsely populated.
short.answer: Very little rain and no water, and thick forests, swamps or steep land. Accept game parks or few roads.

short.q: Explain the difference between clustered and scattered settlement.
short.answer: Clustered means homes are close together in a group, for example around a town. Scattered means homes are far apart from each other.
short.working: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for a clear contrast.

short.q: A dot map has 1 dot for every 1,000 people. A town has 12 dots and a dry area has 2 dots. How many more people live in the town? Show your working.
short.answer: 10,000 more people.

short.q: A bar graph shows sub-county A has 40 thousand people and sub-county B has 25 thousand. Find the total population of the two sub-counties.
short.answer: 65 thousand, which is 65,000 people.
short.working: 40 + 25 = 65 thousand. 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for 65 thousand, 1 mark for 65,000.

short.q: Describe how to draw a dot map showing population distribution in your county.
short.answer: Draw the county boundary. Decide how many people one dot stands for. Put more dots where more people live and fewer dots where few live. Add a title and key.

short.q: Explain why many families live near towns and rivers.
short.answer: Towns have jobs, schools and shops. Rivers give water for drinking and farming. These things make life easier.
short.working: 1 mark for towns, 1 mark for rivers, 1 mark for making life easier.

short.q: Explain why herding communities live in sparsely populated areas.
short.answer: The land is dry, so it cannot support many farms. Herders move with their animals to look for water and grass. So only a few people stay in one place.

short.q: Describe three problems that crowded areas can have and one way of reducing each.
short.answer: Shortage of houses: build more houses. Litter: organise cleaning and waste collection. Traffic: improve roads and public transport. Award marks for each problem and each solution.
short.working: 1 mark for each problem/solution pair, up to 5 marks.

short.q: Name the six aspects of traditional culture.
short.answer: Dressing, food, housing, artefacts, sports and games, and festivals and ceremonies.
short.working: 3 marks for all six, 2 marks for four or five, 1 mark for two or three.

short.q: Give two traditional foods and say where each is popular.
short.answer: For example: githeri in central Kenya and fish with ugali near Lake Victoria. Accept other correct examples.
short.working: 1 mark for each food and 1 mark for each correct place.

short.q: Explain why traditional culture is important.
short.answer: It gives identity, teaches values, and brings people together.

short.q: Explain why some cultural practices are no longer kept.
short.answer: Some practices harm people, such as female genital mutilation and early marriage. The law forbids them. We keep the good parts and leave out the harmful ones.
short.working: 1 mark for harm, 1 mark for law, 1 mark for keeping good parts.

short.q: Describe the houses of two communities in Kenya.
short.answer: The Maasai build low houses of wooden frames covered with mud and dung inside a fence called a manyatta. Old coastal houses in Lamu were built of coral stone with carved doors.
short.working: 1 mark for each community and 1 mark for each description.

short.q: Give three examples of artefacts and say how each is used.
short.answer: A clay pot for cooking or storing water, a basket for carrying items, and a stool for sitting. Accept other correct examples.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct artefact with use.

short.q: Describe how to interview an elder about traditional culture politely.
short.answer: Greet the elder respectfully, ask permission before recording or taking photographs, listen without interrupting, and say thank you.

short.q: Explain the difference between a ceremony and a festival and give one example of each.
short.answer: A ceremony marks a special event in life, such as a wedding. A festival is a big celebration with many people, such as the Lamu Cultural Festival.
short.working: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each example.

short.q: Plan a class culture day. State five things you would include.
short.answer: Traditional dress, foods to taste, songs and dances, artefacts on display, and stories told by elders.

short.q: List four questions you could ask to find out the history of your school.
short.answer: When was the school started? Who started it? Who was the first headteacher? How has the school changed?

short.q: Name two places where you can find information about your school's history.
short.answer: The headteacher or teachers, and the school records or log book. Accept old photographs or elders.

short.q: Give three school values and say why each is important.
short.answer: Honesty helps us to be trusted. Respect keeps peace. Responsibility helps us to do our duties. Accept other valid values.
short.working: 1 mark for each value with a reason.

short.q: Write a short motto and explain what it asks pupils to do.
short.answer: For example: Work hard, be kind. It asks pupils to study well and treat others with kindness.
short.working: 1 mark for a short motto, 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for showing action.
